findings.reason: the plan should name `fleet_node.py` as the owner to extend, or state why its reader cannot serve dispatch, so two sources of truth about "the fleet record" cannot drift the way its own §8 comment warns the retired `max_concurrent_runs` count would.
findings.text: `_fleet_record_path`, `_read_fleet_record` and `_runs_inside_fleet_allocation` re-derive the fleet record's location (`XDG_STATE_HOME`/`~/.local/state/fleet/record.json`) and re-match the job id against `SLURM_JOB_ID`, while `reckon/crew/fleet_node.py:299` (`recorded_job_id`) and `:315` (`find_allocation`) already own reading the fleet record and resolving the allocation this process belongs to

findings.reason: without the comparison a reader cannot tell the FIFO handshake from a duplicate of placement, and the reviewer below either re-opens the same question or rebuilds `placement_argv`.
findings.text: the FIFO `spawn` lane is a second "start a command in the fleet allocation's job" path beside the existing owner `reckon/crew/fleet_node.py:326` (`placement_argv`, `srun --overlap --jobid=<id> ...`) that `reckon fleet-node place` already exposes; the plan never cites `placement_argv` nor says why it cannot be extended (the likely reason — an `srun --overlap` client stays in the caller's step, so it would die with the step — is the load-bearing justification and belongs in the text)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the per-run supervisor hides a substantial sequence (boundary snapshot, spawn, wait, exit-record) behind the "dispatch returns once the supervisor runs" interface, and `supervisor_main.py` keeps the launch vector out of the already-imported package.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the §10 launch half in `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` re-reads the fleet record and re-decides "does this process run inside the allocation" instead of extending the reader/placement owner in `reckon/crew/fleet_node.py`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searches the codebase and cites the mechanism it extends for each change: the tree snapshot and `_tree_state` in `reckon/crew/routing.py`, `stream_paths_newest_first` in `reckon/crew/recovery.py`, `_remove_worktree`/`_release_run_workspace` for worktree release, and the fleet readers in `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py`; it also commissioned a reuse map (`s21-reuse-map`, 73 citations resolved, MISS=0).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the `spawn` verb forwards the spec's `argv` verbatim, but it adds the batch-step process-parenting the design exists to obtain, and the plan states why the launch must leave the session step rather than wrap the forked path.
